title: 1.3 Making of Physics Knowledge
description: Experiential and non-experiential knowledge, and the scientific method

questions.question: Which source of experiential knowledge is described as the dominant source?
Which source of experiential knowledge is described as a "sixth sense" that looks into the most intimate parts of our minds?
Which source of experiential knowledge acts like a recording device that captures events in the order they occur?
Accepting knowledge from what other people report is the source of experiential knowledge called:
Which of the following is a source of experiential knowledge?
How is scientific (physics) knowledge constructed?
options: Through experience, observation, and the scientific method
questions.correctAnswer: Through experience, observation, and the scientific method

questions.question: Introspection allows us to:
options: Record events in the order they occur
Gather information by seeing and touching
Accept knowledge from what others report
Inspect how we are feeling and how our thoughts are operating
questions.correctAnswer: Inspect how we are feeling and how our thoughts are operating

questions.question: Describing your own pain to a doctor is an example of which source of experiential knowledge?
According to the textbook, memory captures events:
options: Only after many years have passed
More or less in the order they occur
Only when they are repeated twice
questions.correctAnswer: More or less in the order they occur

questions.question: When judging testimony, which type of source is usually more reliable?
options: Stories passed down by word of mouth

questions.question: The reliability of testimony depends much on the integrity of the author, the publisher, and the:
options: Language in which it is written
Number of pages in the book

questions.question: Experiential knowledge comes from:
Non-experiential knowledge is best described as:
options: Knowledge gained by hearing others speak
Knowledge not gained through the senses
Knowledge gained by touch and taste
questions.correctAnswer: Knowledge not gained through the senses

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of non-experiential knowledge?
options: Feeling the texture of a stone
Seeing the color of a flower

questions.question: Axioms that are assumed without sensory evidence are a form of:
The scientific method is best described as:
options: A single step of guessing an answer
A way of memorizing facts quickly
A method of recording events from memory
An ordered series of steps to acquire knowledge based on experimental evidence
questions.correctAnswer: An ordered series of steps to acquire knowledge based on experimental evidence

questions.question: What is the first step of the scientific method?
After making observations, what is the second step of the scientific method?
options: Ask a question and identify a problem
questions.correctAnswer: Ask a question and identify a problem

questions.question: The third step of the scientific method is to form a hypothesis, which is:
options: A proposed explanation and a testable prediction
The final answer to the problem
The data collected from an experiment
A list of observations from nature
questions.correctAnswer: A proposed explanation and a testable prediction

questions.question: What is the fourth step of the scientific method?
options: Design and conduct a controlled experiment
questions.correctAnswer: Design and conduct a controlled experiment

questions.question: What is the fifth step of the scientific method?
What is the sixth step of the scientific method?
options: Draw a conclusion that confirms or refutes the hypothesis
questions.correctAnswer: Draw a conclusion that confirms or refutes the hypothesis

questions.question: What is the final step of the scientific method?
In the textbook example, what does the scientist decide to do when studying altitude and boiling water?
options: Measure the amount of water evaporated at one altitude
Cool water at different altitudes and record the freezing point
Test the taste of boiled water at sea level
Heat water at different altitudes and record the boiling temperature
questions.correctAnswer: Heat water at different altitudes and record the boiling temperature

questions.question: According to the textbook data table, at what altitude does water boil at 98 °C?
In the textbook experiment, what is the boiling temperature of water at 0 m altitude?
What conclusion follows from the boiling-point-at-altitude data table?
options: As altitude increases, the boiling point of water decreases
As altitude increases, the boiling point of water increases
The boiling point of water is constant at every altitude
Altitude has no effect on the boiling point of water
questions.correctAnswer: As altitude increases, the boiling point of water decreases

questions.question: Why does the boiling point of water decrease at higher altitudes?
options: Higher atmospheric pressure at higher altitude lowers the boiling point
Lower atmospheric pressure at higher altitude lowers the boiling point
The water is heated faster at higher altitudes
The water contains more impurities at higher altitudes
questions.correctAnswer: Lower atmospheric pressure at higher altitude lowers the boiling point
